hello.note: Also means goodbye and peace. Friends often just say hi (hai)

good-morning.note: The usual reply is בוקר אור (BO-ker OR), morning of light

goodbye.note: Bye (bai) is very common, and shalom works too

please.note: Also means you're welcome and here you are

thank-you.note: תודה רבה (to-DA ra-BA) means thank you very much

excuse-me.note: Also means sorry, and gets a waiter's attention

my-name.note: Literally "they call me", and the same for a man or a woman. The audio uses Peter as the example name

speak-slowly.note: Literally "is it possible to speak slower?" אפשר (ef-SHAR) and a verb is a polite way to ask for anything, and it is the same whoever you ask

speak-english.note: Literally "is English spoken here?", the same whoever you ask. Most Israelis speak English

one.note: The form for counting and prices. Before a masculine word it is אחד (e-KHAD)

how-much.note: For more than one item: כמה הם עולים (KA-ma hem o-LIM)?

would-like.note: The polite way to order. Written the same by a man or a woman, but said differently. The audio uses קפה (ka-FE), coffee, as the example

i-want.note: More direct than ha-YI-ti ro-TSE. Written the same by a man or a woman, but said differently. The audio uses את זה (et ZE), this one, as the example

do-you-have.note: Literally "do you all have", the usual way to ask in a shop. The audio uses מים (MA-yim), water, as the example

ill-take-it.note: The same for a man or a woman

discount.note: Haggling is normal in markets such as the shuk (SHOOK), not in shops

card.note: אשראי (ash-RAI) means credit. Cards are taken almost everywhere

breakfast.note: Israeli hotel breakfasts are famously big

toilet.note: איפה (ey-FO) means where. Put it before any place to ask where it is

taxi.note: Literally "can a taxi be ordered for me?"

airport.note: Ben Gurion airport is usually called נתב״ג (NAT-bag)

bus-station.note: The central bus station. A bus stop is תחנת אוטובוס (ta-kha-NAT O-to-bus)

which-train.note: ל (le) means to, and is joined to the front of the place name. The audio uses חיפה (KHAI-fa), Haifa, as the example

buy-ticket.note: Literally "where does one buy a ticket?"

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Haifa as the example city

trip-length.note: The audio uses Haifa as the example city

delicious.note: Describes the food, so it is the same for a man or a woman

allergic.note: Add the food: פירות ים (pey-ROT YAM) seafood, אגוזים (e-go-ZIM) nuts, ביצים (bei-TSIM) eggs. The audio uses seafood as the example

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.note: For more people: לשלושה (lish-lo-SHA), 3, or לארבעה (le-ar-ba-A), 4

recommend.note: Literally "what is recommended?", the same whoever you ask

beer.note: Beer on tap is בירה מהחבית (BI-ra me-ha-kha-VIT)

coffee.note: Everyday milky coffee is הפוך (ha-FUKH), literally upside-down

help.note: Shout it. The police are משטרה (mish-ta-RA), on 100

pharmacy.note: Many people just name the big chain, סופר-פארם (SU-per farm)
